setlist.title: Beat It On Down The Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Brokedown Palace** (2 reviews): Reviewer singles out the redone Brokedown Palace as a memorable moment; Reviewer states Brokedown Palace was the encore on this date, not on 9/7 [29][37]
- **Beat It On Down The Line** (1 other source): Recording has level variation from PA and recorder at the start, and misses several seconds [4]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Reviewer likes the Scarlet to Fire transition but finds too much cowbell [35]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (1 review): Scarlet Begonias into Fire On The Mountain rocks, according to the reviewer [27]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Reviewer enjoyed echoes spinning around during Estimated Prophet and Space [35]

## Setlist highlights

- **05/85 - Thursday**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [38]

## The recordings

- **gd1985-09-05.dts.mtx.tobin.102049.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 155 min [1]
- **gd1985-09-05.153178.akgc422.davis-holbrook.flac2448**: source not stated; 20 songs; 145 min [4]. Said about its sound: Wind is audible throughout the second set despite factory windscreens [4]
- **gd85-09-05.aud.barbella.11493.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 150 min; rated 4/5 by 4 [15]. Said about its sound: Phil's bass is prominent and booming throughout the audience recording; Reviewer calls the audience recording merely average and advises sampling it before downloading; Static during Let It Grow ruins that song on the audience recording [27][28][32]
- **gd1985-09-05.167116.nak300.mattes.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 147 min [16]
- **gd1985-09-05.163566.neumann.km84i.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 144 min [18]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended on psychedelics, finding the sandstone venue surreal, and felt the band was also in an altered state [26]
- Weather was beautiful; the band played day shows at Red Rocks because of frequent rainouts at night [34]
- Reviewer's group drove from Chicago in a caravan, staying at a brother's place [34]
- Reviewer says the second set opened with a flubbed start that the band restarted, calling it a mulligan [35]
- Reviewer attended all three day shows at Red Rocks that run [36]
- Reviewer's first Dead show; staring at the rocks then looking at the crowd gave everything a greenish cast [37]
- Reviewer finds the Comes a Time from the 9-7-85 show especially sweet and passionate [29]
- Reviewer says the botched Brokedown Palace happened as the encore on 9/7, not at the 9/5 second-set start [36]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1985-09-05.dts.mtx.tobin.102049.flac16**: transferred by Kevin Tobin; source: DTS-Audio-CD 5.1 Mix; SBD (shn id 12180) SBD >> ? > CDR > EAC > SHN + AUD1 (shn id 79778) Sennheiser 441s (7-9 feet high) > Sony D5 > Maxell MX 90s; Tapers:… [1]
- **gd1985-09-05.153178.akgc422.davis-holbrook.flac2448**: taped by Executive Crew; Mike Davis, Kenny Davis, Sean Murtha, Kyle Holbrook, Tom Pinney; transferred by Kyle Holbrook; source: Microphones: s1: AKG C422 (Cardioid) > AKG S42 XY 90º s2: Beyer m201 (hypercardioid) XY 90º Recorder: Sony TC-D5M Location: last row OTS- 120' from stage; 25… [4]. Also: AKG c422 mics became intermittent from wind distortion in set 1, so Beyer m201s replaced them for set 2 [4]
- **gd85-09-05.aud.barbella.11493.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [15]
- **gd1985-09-05.167116.nak300.mattes.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Ted Mattes' Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 300 mics > Sony D5M [16]. Also: A Schoeps source supplies short patches in the Big River to Peggy-O transition, the Let It Grow noodle, and Drums [16]
- **gd1985-09-05.163566.neumann.km84i.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Chris Hecht; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Chris Hecht's Master Audience Cassettes; Neumann KM84i mics > Sony D5M [18]. Also: Mattes's Nakamichi 300 source supplies patches including the Cold Rain and Snow opening, Me and My Uncle, and Drums [18]

claims.text: Reviewer attended on psychedelics, finding the sandstone venue surreal, and felt the band was also in an altered state
Scarlet Begonias into Fire On The Mountain rocks, according to the reviewer
Phil's bass is prominent and booming throughout the audience recording
Reviewer calls the audience recording merely average and advises sampling it before downloading
Reviewer singles out the redone Brokedown Palace as a memorable moment
Reviewer finds the Comes a Time from the 9-7-85 show especially sweet and passionate
Static during Let It Grow ruins that song on the audience recording
Weather was beautiful; the band played day shows at Red Rocks because of frequent rainouts at night
Reviewer's group drove from Chicago in a caravan, staying at a brother's place
Reviewer says the second set opened with a flubbed start that the band restarted, calling it a mulligan
Reviewer likes the Scarlet to Fire transition but finds too much cowbell
Reviewer enjoyed echoes spinning around during Estimated Prophet and Space
Reviewer says the botched Brokedown Palace happened as the encore on 9/7, not at the 9/5 second-set start
Reviewer attended all three day shows at Red Rocks that run
Reviewer's first Dead show; staring at the rocks then looking at the crowd gave everything a greenish cast
Reviewer states Brokedown Palace was the encore on this date, not on 9/7
Wind is audible throughout the second set despite factory windscreens
AKG c422 mics became intermittent from wind distortion in set 1, so Beyer m201s replaced them for set 2

Ted Mattes made the master cassette; Charlie Miller transferred it and coordinated the effort

Chris Hecht made the master cassette; Charlie Miller handled the transfer and coordination
Mattes's Nakamichi 300 source supplies patches including the Cold Rain and Snow opening, Me and My Uncle, and Drums
